subject: Arbor Labs integration — structured-output qualification & SDK/auth checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Greene <alex@arborlabs.ai>, Priya Suresh <priya@arborlabs.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo + next steps — integration notes and immediate asks

Thanks again for the demo this morning — appreciate the product walk-through, Alex and Priya. Quick post-call recap and what we need to keep momentum: 

- Objective: Evaluate Redwood for low-latency on-prem inference for Arbor's clinical triage assistant; initial scope: chat + structured JSON outputs for diagnostic suggestions + embeddings for search/retrieval.
- Key success criteria you mentioned: 95th pct latency < 220ms at 1.5k TPS equivalent, schema-enforced outputs with <1% validation failures, audit logs for generation inputs.

Immediate asks from our side (for the follow-up tech call):
1) SDK & auth: Which SDK language will you use? We can provide Node/Python samples for SRP-based auth (short-lived keys + KMS integration). If you require mutual TLS for Private deployment, confirm cert rotation policy.
2) Routing & failover: Clarify expected geo routing (single us-west region for pilot?) and whether you want model fallback to smaller quantized variant on overload.
3) Structured output: Please share the canonical schema for the clinical JSON output (fields, enums, max_items). We propose constrained decoding + two-layer validation (decoder constraints + schema validator) and a retry policy for nonconformant outputs.

Attached is our integration checklist (+ proposed schema template) for your engineers to review.

Next steps: Can we lock in a 60-minute technical scoping call with your infra and backend lead next Tue 10–11am PT?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: arbor-integration-checklist.pdf (7 pages)
From: Alex Greene <alex@arborlabs.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya@arborlabs.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo + next steps — integration notes and immediate asks

Marissa — great summary, thanks. Quick answers and clarifications: 

- SDKs: Backend team will start with Python. We also have a Node microservice in front that might call Redwood.
- Auth: We prefer short-lived API keys issued by our vault (HashiCorp), and mutual TLS for anything inside our VPC. We can do KMS for key wrapping if required.
- Routing: Pilot will be us-west initially, then us-east for redundancy. Fallback to a quantized variant is acceptable as long as we get deterministic behavior on round trip.
- Schema: Priya will attach the current clinical-output schema (it’s a draft). Expect fields for 'observations', 'differential' (array), 'confidence' (decimal), and 'recommended_actions' with nested enums.

We can do Tue 10–11am PT — I’ll invite our infra lead (Rajiv) and backend (Sara). Please include any pre-read we should review.

—Alex
Alex Greene
Head of Product | Arbor Labs

Thanks Alex — confirming Tue 10–11am PT works. Quick pre-read items for your team to accelerate the scoping call: 

1) Attached: structured-output-schema-proposal.yaml — we filled gaps for max array lengths, enum lists, and string length bounds. Please treat this as a proposed contract; we’ll iterate.
2) Decoder constraints we recommend: top-k/top-p limits and hard token constraints (no free-text outside allowed fields). We’ll show how constrained decoding + reranker/validator flow reduces validation failures.
3) Retry policy:
   - If validator fails transiently (decoder produced out-of-schema but likely recoverable), we recommend one automated retry with altered sampling temperature/decoding constraints.
   - If failure repeats, mark the item for human review and emit structured error with failure_code + raw_model_tokens for auditing.
4) Embeddings/reranker: For recall-sensitive flows, we recommend pre-computed context embeddings + candidate reranker using a cross-encoder on Redwood Dedicated when available.

Dev and Marcus — can you surface (brief bullets) on Tue:
- Dev: sample Python auth flow (vault -> short-lived key -> call Redwood SDK + example of header signing)
- Marcus: expected SLOs for quantized fallback and a short demo of the validator + retry harness (script)

Alex — we’ll include the pre-reads in the calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa

Quick tech notes (to bring to the scoping call):

- Python SDK auth:
  1) Vault issues short-lived token -> exchange with Redwood token broker endpoint (mutual-TLS optional)
  2) SDK code sample (one-liner): client = Redwood(client_token=token, timeout=12.0)
  3) We recommend rotating tokens every 1 hour for pilot; support 15m–24h as options.

- Constrained decoding + validator pattern:
  1) Constrain tokenizer to allowed token sets for field labels; use token-level stop sequences for embedded free-text fields.
  2) Run a JSON schema validator (we provide a Rust/Python validator) immediately after generation. If validator fails due to formatting, autoswitch to a deterministic decoding mode (greedy or beam with forced keys) and retry once.
  3) Emit metrics: validation_failures_total, validation_retry_success_total, validation_permanent_failures_total.

- Retry policy details:
  * Attempt 0: sampling (t=0.2) with constrained tokens
  * Attempt 1 (if schema fail): deterministic decode (beam=5) + forced keys for required fields
  * Attempt 2 (optional, if still failing and marked transient): route to lightweight reranker that can correct structure (costly) or send to human queue depending on severity threshold.

- Fallback SLOs for quantized model: we can guarantee consistent output schema; latency target will be ~30–40% faster cost per token but slightly higher 95th pct variance. Marcus will present numbers Wednesday morning.

I’ll post the SDK snippet and a small harness script to the shared doc before the call.

—Dev
